clue.text: Procures, or seeks to exchange, items of kitchen equipment

indicators.note: the letters of the first three words are to be swapped around, exchanged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone acquires, or tries to trade, various kitchen gadgets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchange' rearranges PROCURES, OR and SEEKS, fifteen letters, into the two-word answer; 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: These sealed pots cook food fast under steam, so they are standard kitchen appliances.

clue.text: Those responsible for road works?

parts.note: road works suggests labourers digging up the highway, but here the works are artworks chalked on the walkway beside a road

explanation.surface: A question about who carries out repairs on the roads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Works' reads as repairs; it is pictures drawn on the pedestrian walkway, which in British English is the pavement (US sidewalk).
explanation.definitionFit: Street performers who chalk pictures on the walkway produce works of art on the road's edge.

clue.text: Take out additional cover for client

parts.note: something additional is extra

indicators.note: the cover of a word is its outside, so the first and last letters of client are taken

explanation.surface: An insurer is asked to remove a top-up policy for a customer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cover for' takes the first and last letters of 'client', C and T; 'additional cover' looks like an insurance term.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull something out or remove it is a synonym phrase for this verb.

clue.text: Island's small rescue vessel?

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
Noah's ark was the boat that saved the animals from the Flood

explanation.surface: A question about an island's little lifeboat.
explanation.definitionFit: Sark is one of the Channel Islands, between England and France.

clue.text: Superior relatives called around

indicators.note: the word for called goes around, enclosing, the word for relatives

parts.note: to have called someone on the phone is to have rang them, as in rang up
kin are one's family members

explanation.surface: Family members of higher status phoned all round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'called' is past tense, so it gives rang rather than call; 'around' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior or highest-placed officer is the ranking one, so the adjective means senior.

clue.text: Boasted about new teeth after visit to the dentist?

definitions.text: teeth after visit to the dentist?

indicators.note: the word for boasted is placed about, around, the letter for new

parts.note: to crow is to brag, so boasted gives crowed

explanation.surface: Someone bragged about their new teeth after a dental appointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' places N inside CROWED. The definition is a whimsical description: teeth that have been capped by a dentist.
explanation.definitionFit: A dentist may fit artificial caps on damaged molars, which are then said to be capped this way.

clue.text: Chooses to stop working

indicators.note: the letters of stop are worked over, rearranged into another order

explanation.surface: Someone decides to give up their job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges STOP; 'to' is only a link. 'to stop working' reads as retiring.
explanation.definitionFit: To pick or select one option is to make a choice, which this verb means.

clue.text: Transport for family member that won't start

indicators.note: a word that will not start loses its first letter, here the R of the relative

parts.note: a relation is a member of one's family

explanation.surface: Someone needs a car for a relative whose vehicle has broken down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that won't start' drops the first letter of RELATION. 'Transport' seems to mean a vehicle but is the noun for rapture.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in transports of joy is a state of rapture, so transport means great happiness.

clue.text: With wisden you might get even!

definitions.text: With wisden you might get even!

parts.words: With wisden you might get even!
parts.note: Wisden is the famous annual cricket almanac packed with past match results, so with it you could look up historical cricket results; getting even is taking revenge

explanation.surface: A claim that a cricket reference book could help you take revenge.
explanation.walkthrough: WISDEN is the yearly cricketers' almanack, full of past match figures; the clue plays on a phrase meaning to take revenge for past wrongs.
explanation.definitionFit: To get even means to repay past grievances, which the idiom describes.

clue.text: Carefully check royal article, being experienced

parts.note: to vet something is to examine it carefully
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the royal cipher of the Queen
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone experienced examines a royal item with care.
explanation.definitionFit: A seasoned hand with long service is an old campaigner, so the word works as an adjective.

clue.text: One excluded ineligible players

parts.note: out can mean not in the running, as in out of contention
the cast is the set of actors in a show

explanation.surface: A rejected person stands among players not allowed to take part.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone shunned or rejected by society is a pariah, left out of the group.

clue.text: Intend workers to welcome answer

indicators.note: to welcome is to take in, so the workers enclose the letter for answer

parts.note: men is a common crossword term for workers or staff
A is a standard abbreviation for answer; the run of letters also spelling the solution across welcome answer is a coincidence, as the container reading uses every word

explanation.surface: A manager plans to have the staff greet a reply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to welcome' places A inside MEN.
explanation.definitionFit: To intend is to have in mind as a purpose, which this verb also means.

clue.text: Grand Prix racing to finish? The devil it is!

parts.note: Formula One, F1, is top-level Grand Prix motor racing, with the digit 1 read as the letter I
an end is a finish

explanation.surface: A motor racing fan exclaims about the outcome of a Grand Prix.
explanation.walkthrough: F1 is written FI, the 1 standing as an I; 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A demon or evil spirit is a word for Satan himself.

clue.text: Key to poor legislation

parts.note: B is a musical key
ill can mean poor or bad, as in ill health

explanation.surface: A remark that the key to a failing law has been found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' is only a link; 'Key' is a musical key, not a solution.
explanation.definitionFit: A draft law put before parliament is a proposed piece of legislation.

clue.text: Turn very old in bed

indicators.note: the letters for very and old are placed in the word for bed

parts.note: pit is British slang for one's bed

explanation.surface: A very old person rolls over in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts V and O inside PIT, British slang for bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To swivel or rotate on a central point is to turn.

clue.text: Ruin the odds on black gold

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the odds offered in horse racing
black gold is a common nickname for crude petroleum

explanation.surface: Betting on crude prices could bring someone to financial ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: SP, the starting price in British betting, gives the odds; 'on' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To damage or wreck something is to mar it, a synonym of ruin.

clue.text: How Washington was dismissed as being of no importance?

indicators.note: how asks in what way, here hinting the letters left over are put into a new order
dismissed means sent away, so the letters of was are removed from the city's name

explanation.surface: A question about how a US president was written off as insignificant.
explanation.walkthrough: Take WAS out of WASHINGTON to leave HINGTON, then rearrange those letters ('How') into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that counts for zero or is worthless can be described as amounting to zero.

clue.text: Help oneself, being keen on chasing pickpocket

indicators.note: chasing means coming behind, so the words for keen on follow the word for pickpocket

parts.note: dip is old slang for a pickpocket
to be into something is to be keen on it

explanation.surface: An enthusiast chases a thief who helps himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being' is only a link; DIP is old thieves' slang, and 'Help oneself' is a phrase verb meaning take some.
explanation.definitionFit: To take freely from a supply, as from a shared fund, is to help yourself.

clue.text: Kennedy perhaps left after broadcast

indicators.note: after means the word for left comes behind the word for broadcast

parts.note: to air something is to broadcast it
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: President Kennedy departs after a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: Kennedy is JFK, the New York air hub, not the president.
explanation.definitionFit: JFK in New York is an example of an international air terminal.

clue.text: Get organised again after Roger failed at university

indicators.note: failed suggests the name has broken down and its letters are to be reordered

parts.note: up means at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: Someone must sort himself out after Roger failed his degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failed' rearranges ROGER; 'after' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To reassemble or rally again is to form up once more.

clue.text: Seaweed the Spanish love with fruit

parts.note: tang is a type of seaweed
el is Spanish for the
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A recipe of seaweed and Spanish love mixed with fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is only a link; love as O comes from tennis scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: A citrus hybrid of tangerine and grapefruit is a type of fruit.

clue.text: Indicated small change on diet plan

parts.note: P, a penny, is a small coin

indicators.note: a plan arranges things, so the letters of on and diet are arranged anew

explanation.surface: A dieter switches a small item in a weight-loss plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'small change' suggests a minor alteration; it is a penny coin, and 'plan' is the anagram signal for the diet words.
explanation.definitionFit: To have shown or gestured towards something is to have indicated it.

clue.text: Commended head of police and gave promotion

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: to raise someone is to promote them

explanation.surface: A police chief praised and promoted an officer.
explanation.definitionFit: To have commended someone is to have spoken well of them, a synonym.

clue.text: In two minds over trouble with wind!

parts.note: to be torn is to be undecided between two options
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: An indecisive person fusses about a wind problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' and 'with' are only links; in a down clue 'over' places TORN above ADO.
explanation.definitionFit: A violent rotating storm is a destructive kind of wind.

clue.text: Marks silver in case of thieves

indicators.note: the symbol for silver is put in the case of the word thieves
the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Silver goods are labelled as being in thieves' hands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'case of' takes the first and last letters of 'thieves', T and S; 'in' puts AG between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Labels or tickets attached to items are identifying marks.

clue.text: Readily available and working, thanks to quiet

parts.note: on means functioning or working
ta is British informal for thanks
p, piano, is the musical notation for quiet

explanation.surface: Something is operational thanks to keeping it quiet.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British slang for thank you; 'and' and 'to' are only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer from the barrel is ready to draw, so the phrase means at hand when wanted.

clue.text: The chap who has an odd earpiece

indicators.note: the odd letters are the first, third, fifth and seventh of the word earpiece

explanation.surface: A man who wears a strange earphone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' takes alternate letters of 'earpiece', starting from the first; 'who has an' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name stands for a particular man, as a fellow or a bloke.

clue.text: Knock up runs for salmon

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for knock reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a rap is a knock
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A cricketer quickly scores runs to win some fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RAP backwards; 'for' is only a link. 'Knock up' looks like a phrase for a quick practice.
explanation.definitionFit: A young fish before it goes to sea is a technical name for an immature salmon.

clue.text: Old Tory leader in charge of hearing

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A former Conservative leader responsible for a public inquiry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearing' looks like a court session; it is the sense, and the answer is the adjective for the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective relates to the ear, so it means auditory.

clue.text: The boards accepted alternative warehousing

indicators.note: to accept is to take in, so the word for the boards encloses the word for alternative

parts.note: the boards is the theatre stage
or introduces an alternative

explanation.surface: The theatre agreed to an alternative warehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The boards' is theatre slang for the stage, as in treading the boards.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping goods in a depot for later use is warehousing.

clue.text: Future outlook of group with reasonable following?

indicators.note: following means the word for reasonable comes after the word for group

parts.note: a set is a group
fair means reasonable or just

explanation.surface: A group with a decent following has good prospects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is only a link. The answer is a barometer forecast, settled weather ahead.
explanation.definitionFit: A barometer's forecast of settled weather ahead gives a fine forecast for days to come.

clue.text: Good leaders that show no resistance?

parts.note: super means excellent or good
conductors lead orchestras

explanation.surface: Excellent orchestra leaders who never meet opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resistance' looks like opposition to a leader; it is electrical resistance.
explanation.definitionFit: Some materials when supercooled carry current with zero electrical resistance.
